Tim Cook's tenure as Apple CEO is entering its final weeks, with John Ternus set to officially take over the helm on September 1. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan believes Ternus could usher in a bolder, more risk-taking new era for Apple.

Ternus is expected to take on greater risks after assuming the CEO role, including launching new products, making acquisitions, and ramping up R&D efforts

Apple's CEO transition is nearly complete. So far, the company has worked hard to emphasize policy continuity under Ternus's leadership.

However, not everyone on Wall Street is convinced that Ternus will simply follow in Cook's footsteps.

According to a research note obtained by The Street, Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan reiterated his strong "Buy" rating on Apple. One of the bank's key reasons for its bullish stance is its expectation that Ternus will both continue Cook's legacy and possess a greater "risk appetite." Moza Faruque writes:

The bank highlighted that Apple's abandonment of its "cash-neutral" target is an early signal that management may be more willing to deploy capital. This would translate into higher R&D spending, more capex, and potentially larger M&A activity—areas that were not dominant strategies during the Cook era. Bank of America believes that under Ternus's leadership, Apple may move more aggressively into entirely new product categories, including AI glasses, AirPods with cameras, smart rings, smart home devices, virtual personal assistants, and robotics.

Overall, Bank of America believes Ternus will continue Cook's legacy of building Apple into a highly profitable global machine, but also expects him to leverage the company's current strong position to make riskier bets going forward.

When Ternus first takes the CEO reins, we likely won't see any dramatic shifts. But over time, differences in priorities between him and Cook may gradually emerge.

What are your expectations for Ternus as Apple's CEO? Let us know in the comments.
